title: Conjunction of polynomial-time predicates
statement: Let $p$ and $q$ be Boolean predicates on binary strings. If the functions sending each input $x$ to the one-bit word $[p(x)]$ and $[q(x)]$ are polynomial-time computable, then so is the function $x\mapsto[p(x)\wedge q(x)]$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ and $q$ are Boolean-valued functions on binary strings
The one-bit output function for $p$ is polynomial-time computable
The one-bit output function for $q$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced:
Let $p$ and $q$ be Boolean predicates on binary strings. If the single-bit functions
$x \mapsto [p(x)]$ and $x \mapsto [q(x)]$ are both polynomial-time computable, then
so is $x \mapsto [p(x) \wedge q(x)]$.
